hints: Look at what telomerase is for in the stem. It prevents telomere loss after many mitotic cycles, so ask yourself which of 1, 2 and 3 must keep dividing again and again.
Remember most normal body cells switch telomerase off and so age, but any cell type that needs unlimited or very rapid repeated mitosis must switch it back on to protect chromosome ends.
walkthrough:
**Recall the telomere problem**

Lovely start. Every time DNA replicates, a little bit of the chromosome end, the telomere, is lost.

Most normal cells do not replace it, so after many divisions they stop dividing. Telomerase rebuilds telomeres to allow more divisions.

**Ask who needs many divisions**

Now think like the cell. Cancer cells divide uncontrollably and forever. Stem cells must keep dividing for life to replace tissues. Activated memory B-lymphocytes must divide very rapidly by clonal expansion to make lots of plasma cells and antibodies.

All three need to avoid telomere loss.

**Conclude all three transcribe telomerase**

So 1, 2 and 3 all need to transcribe the gene for telomerase to stay mitotically active. That matches option A, 1, 2 and 3.

options.A: Correct and well done. Cancer cells, stem cells and activated memory B-lymphocytes all undergo many rapid mitotic cycles, so all need telomerase to maintain telomeres.
options.B: Not complete. It correctly includes 1 and 2 but wrongly leaves out 3, yet activated memory B-lymphocytes also need rapid clonal expansion.
options.C: Not complete. It correctly includes 1 and 3 but wrongly leaves out 2, yet stem cells must divide throughout life and need telomerase.
options.D: Not complete. It correctly includes 2 and 3 but wrongly leaves out 1, yet cancer cells reactivate telomerase to achieve immortality.
